messages:
maria: quick follow-up from yesterday's RFC — i ran a small sim of cross-region leader failover and found a couple of double-charge windows when shards are rebalanced. not huge but reproducible.
aj: ugh. can you paste the minimal repro?
maria: sure — simplified flow: write billing-event -> commitlog ack -> consumer emits charge to accounting. if leader moves before consumer checkpoint, consumer replays and we get dup charges.
sam: is this just late checkpointing or are we missing an idempotency envelope?
maria: it's both. we have event ids but they are local-to-shard. after rebalance the same logical token can land on a different shard with a fresh id.
leo: options: 1) global canonical id generation (e.g., tenant+usage-root-id hash) at producer time, 2) fencing/lease events in the commitlog to mark ownership, 3) consumer-side dedupe table with cross-shard lookups.
aj: 1 is simplest for dedupe but increases producer surface area. 2 gives strong semantics but complicates sharding — need to coordinate fencing high-frequency. 3 is doable but we'd need a low-latency global index (redis/rocksdb+replicas) and strong consistency for correctness.
maria: also concerned about backfills: if we change id scheme later we can't retroactively dedupe older events without heavy backfill work.
sam: what about a small durable "billing-fence" event we emit on rebalance: producer emits normal events, and during shard handoff we write a fence record like {type: "FENCE", shard: X, epoch: 123, wall_time: 1670000000}. consumers treat fence as a checkpoint boundary and reconcile in-flight ids observed after fence. cheap and bounded.
leo: interesting. fence gives a monotonic epoch per shard so even if ids are local you can compare epoch to avoid replaying older local ids from prior owners.
aj: downside: fencing requires an extra write on handoff which increases handoff latency and a small window if handoff crash occurs. need retry logic.
maria: proposal: implement fence + canonical token hash. fences give fast correctness for rebalance; canonical hash ensures long-term dedupe for mixed legacy events. rollout plan: write fence handling in consumer first (safe), then start producing canonical id for new producers, finally add fencing to handoff path.
sam: agree. test matrix: single-shard failover, multi-shard rebalance, simultaneous leader swaps, and backfill replay. also add integration test for cross-region clock skew.\maria: also flagged to billing team that we'll need a small reconciliation job to sweep ambiguous windows for last 7 days post-rollout.\ops-bot: deploy-plan created: PR#2714 -> canary eng-platform (1 shard) -> ramp 10% -> full. ETA 2 weeks. :party-parrot:
leo: one more: metric to add: "fence-applied-latency" and "duplicate-detected-rate" so we can verify improvement.
maria: noted. i'll open the consumer PR today and add a short design note with the rollout steps + tests. thanks everyone.
